notes.meaning: God came to the rescue of His people Israel, reaching out His hand to lift them up when they could not help themselves. He did this because He remembered His promise of mercy made long ago to Abraham and his descendants. The greatest proof of this mercy was sending the promised Messiah to save His people forever.

Mary stayed with Elizabeth for about three months before returning to her home in Nazareth. This extended visit gave both women time to encourage each other and see God's amazing promises taking shape.
Elizabeth reached the full time of her pregnancy and gave birth to a son. God fulfilled His promise to the elderly couple exactly as He had said.

Elizabeth's neighbors and relatives were filled with joy when they heard what had happened. They saw that the Lord had shown her extraordinary kindness by taking away her shame and giving her a child in her old age.

On the eighth day after birth, family and friends gathered to circumcise the baby in obedience to God's law. Because it was customary to name the child at that time, the guests assumed the boy would be named Zechariah after his father.
Elizabeth firmly refused and told them the baby must be named John. She insisted on this because the angel had specifically commanded that name before the boy was conceived.
The relatives objected because no one in their family tree carried that name. They made signs to Zechariah to see what he wanted, showing that he was unable to hear as well as unable to speak.

Zechariah asked for a small wooden tablet covered in wax and wrote, 'His name is John.' He did not treat the choice as an open question, but stated the name as an already settled fact, which astonished the whole crowd.
The moment Zechariah obeyed God's command in writing, his tongue was freed and his speech returned. He immediately used his voice to praise God rather than complain about his months of silence.

A deep, reverent awe fell over all the neighbors when they saw these miraculous events. People throughout the hill country of Judea began talking constantly about what God was doing in Zechariah's family.

Everyone who heard the news thought deeply about it and wondered what kind of leader the child would become. It was plain to see that the Lord's hand—meaning His special favor, protection, and power—was resting on the boy.

Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak as a prophet. His inspired message was not centered on his own family pride, but on the great rescue God was preparing through the coming Messiah.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars doubt that Zechariah composed this poem on the spot, suggesting it was written later by early Jewish Christians or composed by Luke himself.

notes.meaning: Zechariah praised the God of Israel because He had come to visit and redeem His people. To redeem means to pay the price to set captives free, and God was now purchasing freedom for sinners through Jesus.

God raised up a 'horn of salvation' from the family line of King David. In Scripture, a horn represents power and safety, pointing to Christ as a mighty Savior who is strong enough to conquer our enemies and shield those who trust Him.

This great rescue fulfilled what God had promised through His holy prophets across many centuries. From the earliest days of Scripture, these messengers spoke with one unified voice about the coming Savior.
God promised rescue from enemies and from all who hate His people. While many Jews hoped for deliverance from Roman rule, the real enemies being conquered were sin, death, and the power of Satan.

God showed mercy to the ancient fathers by remembering His sacred covenant and the solemn oath He swore to Abraham. Even after long delays, God proved that He never forgets or abandons what He promised to His people.

God rescues His people so they can serve and worship Him without slavish fear. True freedom from spiritual enemies enables believers to live in holiness toward God and justice toward other people throughout their entire lives.

Zechariah turned to his baby boy and called him a prophet of the Most High God. John was appointed to go just ahead of the Lord like a royal herald, preparing the hearts of the people to receive the Messiah.

John was sent to teach the people that true salvation comes through the forgiveness of their sins. God's rescue does not come through political power, but through having our wrongdoing pardoned by God.
This wonderful pardon flows entirely from the tender, heartfelt mercy of God. Because of His compassion, the 'Dawn' or sunrise from heaven visits our dark world in the person of Jesus Christ.

The light of the Savior shines on people trapped in spiritual darkness and living under the shadow of death. By giving this light, Christ safely guides our wandering steps into the road that leads to true peace with God.

Young John grew in bodily strength and spiritual maturity under the guidance of the Holy Spirit. He lived quietly in the wilderness, separated from worldly distractions, until the appointed time came for him to begin his public ministry to Israel.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars suggest John may have spent time with the Essene community near the Dead Sea, though others note that his open preaching to all Israel differed from their strict, isolated group.
